The pt2399-core board BEFORE it was populated: the exact bytes committed by
aa5034b, "pcb: KiCad project and empty 2-layer board for pt2399-core", which is
the commit that created it. Byte-identical to that revision, not re-authored.

WHY A COPY EXISTS AT ALL. The headless update tool refuses a board that already
holds footprints, so its tests need an EMPTY board, and they used to copy
circuits/pt2399-core/pt2399-core.kicad_pcb for that. Running the tool against
the committed board for real - a deliberate act, and the point of the tool -
filled it with 24 footprints, and every one of those tests then refused at
board-not-empty instead of reaching the guard it was written for: 25 tests red
across tests/pcb/update-from-schematic.test.ts and
tests/pcb/update-scratch-retention.test.ts, every one of them a false red.

This file is NOT a reduced or synthetic board. It is the real board's own
configuration - the layer stack, the (setup) block and the DRC floors task 6a
wrote - which is what makes the end-to-end test a test of this circuit rather
than of a toy. The schematic and the .kicad_pro those tests use still come from
circuits/pt2399-core/.

STALENESS IS GUARDED, NOT TRUSTED. A later change to the real board's (setup)
block would leave this fixture testing a configuration the circuit no longer
has. tests/pcb/update-from-schematic.test.ts asserts that no (setup) key here is
absent from the committed board, and that this file still holds zero footprints,
so the drift shows up as a failure rather than as a quietly weaker test.
